securityClaim: No system is 100% secure. This policy targets standards-aligned quantum readiness using free/open-source tooling.
minimumTlsVersionComment: minimumTlsVersion is a TARGET the project aims at, not an enforced floor - server/config/cryptoPolicy.js validates that this field stays TLSv1.3, and nothing in the codebase can actually raise a production edge to TLS 1.3. Every production hostname is platform-assigned (cloudfront.net, vercel.app, netlify.app), so ACM validation cannot be satisfied (none of those zones belong to this project) and a custom certificate, the only way to change a CloudFront viewer minimum, cannot be issued. The protocol floor is set by each provider. Measured 2026-10-15 across the live production edges: floor TLSv1.2, TLS 1.3 offered on every edge, TLS 1.0/1.1 accepted nowhere. So TLS 1.3 is AVAILABLE everywhere and REQUIRED nowhere. The enforceable requirements live in config/security/tls-edge-posture.json and are measured by scripts/security/tls-posture-probe.cjs.
forbiddenNewCrypto: RSA publicEncrypt/privateDecrypt for application payload encryption
warningCrypto: third-party SDK crypto outside direct app control
productionRules: Do not deploy experimental OQS/liboqs TLS directly to production without staging evidence.
Keep rollback to classical TLS 1.3 possible.
Never invent a cryptographic primitive; application-layer composition must use standardized primitives with documented domain separation.

runtimePqc.notes: Application-layer hybrid PQC is implemented with native Node 24.7+/OpenSSL 3.5+ primitives and is opt-in. Field encryption and the security event ledger default to their classical modes so an unconfigured deployment cannot fail closed on a runtime that lacks FIPS 203/204 support. Production rollout requires explicit key references and the require mode.
